processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingots of nominal composition Fe-35Mn-19Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by vacuum induction melting of high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials under an argon atmosphere, then homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h.

Homogenized ingots hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm; plates then cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples by electrical discharge machining for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterization.
Samples solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere followed by oil quenching (parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq).
Solution-treated samples were aged at temperatures between 525 °C and 650 °C for 1, 3, 6 and 10 h, followed by water quenching; this sample corresponds to the 625 °C / 10 h condition.

structures.overall_structure: After aging the 19Al (Fe-35Mn-19Al-5Cu at.%) alloy at 625 °C for 10 h, the α (BCC) matrix has almost completely transformed into β-Mn, with numerous fine BCC and FCC Cu-rich precipitates distributed within the β-Mn at its interfaces.

phases_present.morphology: near-equiaxed grains forming the continuous matrix after the α → β-Mn transformation
fine precipitates within the β-Mn at the β-Mn interfaces
fine particles located at the interfaces between β-Mn

interfaces.phase_evolution: During aging the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels evolve as α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase + α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase. For the 19Al alloy at 600 °C and above the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn within just 1 h.
interfaces.interface_notes: New BCC phase and FCC Cu-rich phase form at the interfaces between the β-Mn in the ultra-hard Fe-Mn-Al-Cu alloys. The content of the FCC Cu-rich phase between β-Mn interfaces decreased gradually with increasing Al content.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness measured with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s, each sample tested 5 times and the average reported; condition: aged at 625 °C for 10 h followed by water quenching

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: load 9.8 N, dwell 15 s, each sample tested 5 times and averaged; specimen surface electrolytically polished (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol)
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers hardness of the 19Al alloy after solution treatment and after each aging treatment (625 °C for 10 h for this sample)
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 19Al alloy aged at 625 °C for 10 h exhibits a Vickers hardness of 869.5 ± 8.6 HV; the solution-treated baseline is 263.8 ± 1.1 HV; the 19Al aging-hardening window spans 263.8–917.8 HV.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: GeminiSEM 300 SEM; scanning step size 1.5 μm (low magnification) and 0.05 μm (high magnification)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: electrolytically polished using a mixture of 10 % perchloric acid and 90 % ethanol
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the constituent phases (α, β-Mn, α-Mn, BCC, FCC Cu-rich) and their evolution with aging in the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu alloys
characterization_methods.key_findings: EBSD on solution-treated alloys shows a single α (BCC) phase; aging produces the α → β-Mn transformation with new BCC and FCC precipitates; in the 19Al alloy the α matrix is almost fully transformed to β-Mn at 600 °C/3 h and 650 °C/6 h.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: electrolytically polished samples (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol)
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn, β-Mn) and new precipitates in the aged Fe-Mn-Al-Cu alloys
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 19Al alloy, at 525 °C the α matrix stays almost featureless even after 10 h; from 550 °C β-Mn appears decorating α grain boundaries and as short rods within grains; at 600 °C and above the α transforms almost completely to β-Mn.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: phase identification of electrolytically polished samples
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the phase compositions of the alloys after aging
characterization_methods.key_findings: Both α-Mn and β-Mn diffraction peaks were found (e.g. 19Al 550 °C × 6 h), indicating α-Mn and β-Mn co-precipitated during aging before full α → β-Mn transformation; α/D0₃ reflections were also present.

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM), SAED, HRTEM and EDS
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Talos F200X microscope equipped with an EDS detector, operated at 200 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: TEM foils mechanically ground to ~90 μm, punched to 3 mm discs and ion thinned
characterization_methods.purpose: Elucidate the fine precipitates at the β-Mn interfaces in the ultra-hard samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fine FCC Cu-rich particles with frequent FCC twins form at the β-Mn interfaces; β-Mn identified by SAED; the FCC phase is rich in Cu, depleted in Fe and Mn and slightly poor in Al. (Characterized on the 15Al 600 °C/6 h and 17Al 575 °C/6 h samples; not performed on the 19Al alloy.)

unmapped_findings: 19Al (Fe-35Mn-19Al-5Cu at.%) EDS-measured chemical composition (Table 1): Fe 41.6, Mn 34.8, Al 18.6, Cu 5.0 (at.%).
The solution-treated baseline Vickers hardness of the 19Al alloy is 263.8 ± 1.1 HV (before aging).

For the hardest 19Al sample (aged at 600 °C for 10 h, 917.8 HV): nanoindentation average hardness = 10.4 ± 1.3 GPa, intrinsic β-Mn hardness = 12.5 ± 0.4 GPa, and β-Mn SEM-EDS composition = Mn 36.2 at.%, Al 17.5 at.%, Cu 2.6 at.%.
The fracture toughness (KIC) of the hardest 19Al sample (600 °C/10 h) is 3.5 MPa·m^1/2, measured by the indentation technique.
The elastic modulus of the 19Al alloy is 181 GPa, measured from compressive stress-strain curves.
The optimal aging temperature window for the 19Al alloy to achieve ultra-high hardness is 575–625 °C.
After aging the 19Al alloy at 525 °C for 10 h only 12.1 % β-Mn had precipitated, giving a minimal hardness increase.

The increase in Al content slowed the precipitation kinetics of β-Mn and decreased the fracture toughness of the ultra-hard Fe-Mn-Al-Cu alloys; the volume fraction of FCC Cu-rich + BCC precipitates in the 19Al alloy aged 650 °C/6 h reached 6.5 % (Vickers hardness 810.9 HV).

The Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels attain a maximum specific hardness exceeding 140 HV·cm³/g (the 15Al alloy reached 141 HV·cm³/g), higher than existing steels and M/HEAs (usually below 120 HV·cm³/g).
